summary:
Cellular Sentinel is a conceptual spaceflight health monitoring architecture that bridges comparative zoology with astronaut biomarker telemetry to detect early radiation-induced DNA damage and immune suppression during deep-space missions. Outside Earth's magnetosphere, astronauts face chronic Galactic Cosmic Radiation (GCR), Solar Particle Events (SPEs), and microgravity, which degrade cellular stability long before standard vital signs show clinical symptoms.
Grounded in evolutionary radiotolerance mechanisms—specifically the Damage Suppressor (Dsup) chromatin-shielding protein in tardigrades (Ramazzottius varieornatus) and amplified TP53 tumor-suppression pathways in African elephants (Loxodonta africana)—Cellular Sentinel establishes predictive diagnostic thresholds for human cells. The modular software pipeline integrates ambient radiation telemetry (NASA Rad Lab/OSDR) with microfluidic capillary blood biomarkers (lymphocyte counts, 8-OHdG oxidative stress, and γ-H2AX double-strand DNA breaks) and Gene Lab multi-omics baselines. Through a three-tier alert dashboard (Green, Yellow, Red), the system empowers crews to execute timely countermeasures—such as antioxidant protocols or radiation storm-shelter relocation—during communication delays with Earth.
details: Cellular Sentinel is a conceptual spaceflight health monitoring software architecture that bridges comparative evolutionary zoology with astronaut biomarker telemetry to detect early microscopic DNA damage and immune shifts during long-duration deep-space missions. Developed as a solo no-code architectural and UI prototype using NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), GeneLab multi-omics, RadLab radiation models, and Standard Measures datasets, the system integrates ambient radiation dosimetry with microfluidic blood biomarkers (lymphocyte counts, 8-OHdG oxidative stress, and \(\gamma \)-H2AX double-strand breaks). Its creative diagnostic logic calibrates human cellular thresholds against natural radiotolerance mechanisms—specifically the chromatin-shielding Dsup protein in tardigrades (Ramazzottius varieornatus) and amplified TP53 tumor-suppressor pathways in African elephants (Loxodonta africana). Designed around communication delays with Earth, low crew cognitive load, and compact space-compatible blood assays, the three-panel dashboard delivers autonomous Green, Yellow, and Red health alerts with clear countermeasures—protecting astronauts on lunar and Mars missions while offering transferable diagnostic logic for occupational radiation monitoring and early cancer detection on Earth.
